speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to begin my assessment, how would you describe the nature and onset of this pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned a history of recurrent urinary tract infections; have you noticed any fever, chills, or burning sensation during urination alongside the blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of recurrent urinary tract infections is concerning for a potential underlying structural issue or stone; have you noticed any passage of small, hard objects in your urine or gravel-like material? Additionally, are you experiencing any nausea, vomiting, or fever at this time?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. To further characterize your pain and rule out other causes, does the discomfort radiate toward your groin or testicle, and has it come on suddenly and severely? Also, have you noticed any clots in your urine or pain that comes and goes in waves?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
